items.text: Summary ($A$ a direct sum of projectives of finite type): a coalgebra structure with counit on $A$ = a continuous algebra structure on $H=A^\vee$; a left comodule structure on $M$ = a left $H$-module structure with $s\mapsto sx$ continuous for each $x$.
Subcomodules and quotient comodules
$A$ a coalgebra, $M$ a left comodule, $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$.
$M\to M''$ surjective, so $V(M'')\hookrightarrow V(M)$.
$M''$ is stable (a quotient comodule) if $V(M'')\subset V(M)$ is a $V(A)$-submodule; equivalently $\delta_M$ induces $\delta_{M''}$:
\begin{CD} M @>{\delta_M}>> M\otimes A\\ @VVV @VVV\\ M'' @>{\delta_{M''}}>> M''\otimes A \end{CD}
Unit and associativity then hold on $M''$ automatically.
For $M'\hookrightarrow M$: $V(M)\to V(M')$ need not be surjective, and $M'\otimes A\to M\otimes A$ need not be injective; use $W(M')\to W(M)\to W(M'')\to0$ (right exact).
$M'$ has an induced comodule structure if there is $M'\to M'\otimes A$ making $M'\to M$ a morphism of comodules; unique if $M'\otimes A\to M\otimes A$ is injective.
\begin{CD} M' @>>> M'\otimes A\\ @VVV @VVV\\ M @>{\delta_M}>> M\otimes A \end{CD}
When $M'\otimes A\to M\otimes A$ is injective, $M'$ stable $\iff$ $M''$ stable.
Injectivity holds if $A$ is flat over $k$ (then stable submodules are stable under sums and finite intersections), or $M''$ flat, or $M'$ a direct factor.
For a monoid $G$: left comodules over $A$ = $k$-modules with $G$ operating on the left; a stable quotient (resp. submodule) = one on which $G$ operates compatibly.
$A$ flat and a direct sum of projectives of finite type (over a field, say): $M'\subset M$ is stable iff it is an $H$-submodule.
Corollaries
(1) For $M'\subset M$ there is a smallest stable submodule containing $M'$: the sub-$H$-module generated by $M'$.
If $M'$ is of finite type over $k$, so is this submodule: $Hx$, image of $s\mapsto sx$, factors through some $A_\alpha^\vee$, projective of finite type.
\overline{x}=Hx=\text{smallest submodule }N\subset M\ \text{with}\ \delta(x)\in N\otimes A
(2) Every comodule is a filtering direct limit of subcomodules of finite type over $k$. For a monoid $G$ (over a field): every $G$-module is a union of finite-dimensional $G$-stable subspaces.
$A$ as a bicomodule
$A$ is a comodule over itself on the left and on the right (by $\pi$, resp. $\pi$ composed with the symmetry): $V(A)$ acts on itself on both sides.
(3) For $B\subset A$ there is a smallest sub-bimodule $B^{V(A)}\supset B$ stable under left and right operations; finite over $k$ if $B$ is.
\pi(B)\subset B\otimes A\ \ (\text{left}),\qquad \pi(B)\subset A\otimes B\ \ (\text{right})
$A/B$ flat $\Rightarrow$ $(B\otimes A)\cap(A\otimes B)=B\otimes B$, so $B$ stable on both sides iff $\pi(B)\subset B\otimes B$: $B$ is a subcoalgebra.
(4) Over a field every coalgebra is the filtering direct limit of subcoalgebras of finite dimension; dually
H=\varprojlim A_i^\vee,\quad A_i^\vee\ \text{finite algebras, transitions and projections surjective}
Algebraic groups over a field
Proposition. $k$ a field, $G$ an affine algebraic monoid (resp. group). Then
(a) $G=\varprojlim G_i$, a filtering inverse limit of affine monoids (resp. groups) $G_i$ of finite type;
(b) if $G$ is of finite type $G$ is a closed submonoid of $\underline{\operatorname{End}}(M)$ (resp. a closed subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_n$, for $G$ a group) for suitable $M$, $n=\dim M$.

Proof of (a). $A=\varinjlim M_i$, $M_i$ finite subcoalgebras; $A_i$ = the $k$-algebra generated by $M_i$ in $A$: of finite type, stable under left and right translations, so a bialgebra, a monoid $G_i$:
A=\varinjlim A_i\ \Longleftrightarrow\ G=\varprojlim G_i

$G$ a group, $\sigma$ the antipode ($\sigma^2=1$): $M+\sigma(M)$ is stable under both translations if $M$ is; so the $M_i$, hence the $A_i$, can be taken stable under $\sigma$, and the $G_i$ are groups.
Proof of (b). $A$ of finite type: choose a finite $M\subset A$ generating $A$ as an algebra, stable under left translations; $G$ acts linearly on $M$:
\rho\colon G\to\underline{\operatorname{End}}(M)\ \ (\mathrm{GL}_n\ \text{for a group});\qquad \rho\ \text{is a closed immersion: }\ k[\operatorname{End}M]\to A\ \text{surjective}
Its image contains $M$: for $\varphi\in M$ and $g\in G(k')$,
(g\varphi)(e)=\varphi(g\cdot e)=\varphi(g)
$\varphi$ is a matrix coefficient of the representation on $M$ (evaluation at $e$ is a linear form); $M$ generates $A$, so the map is surjective.
